exam.subject: History
exam.title: Eritrean Secondary Education Certificate Examinations 2018 History

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements is **incorrect**?

options.A: History helps us to be proud of our culture and national identity.
options.B: The period before writing was developed is known as pre-history.
options.C: History can be written without a source.
options.D: Letters, treaties, tools and paintings are examples of primary sources.
options.E: Primary sources are firsthand accounts of an event.

explanation_steps: History is the study of the past based on evidence. It cannot be written without sources. Sources are the 'raw materials' of history; without them, there is no way to verify what happened.

questions.stem: The Romans who came after the Greeks

options.B: failed to create a large empire of their own.
options.C: preserved and transmitted aspects of Greek civilization.
options.D: succeeded in building a democratic system like Athens.

explanation_steps: The Romans greatly admired Greek culture (art, philosophy, and science). They adopted and adapted many Greek elements, creating what is known as Graeco-Roman civilization, which they then spread throughout their vast empire.

questions.stem: One of the effects of the crusades was the

options.C: weakening of kings and the growing stronger of nobles.

explanation_steps: The Crusades led to the revival of trade and learning in Europe as contact with the Byzantine and Islamic worlds increased. Politically, they weakened feudalism (nobles died or sold land to join) and strengthened kings, paving the way for centralized nation-states.

questions.stem: Identify the **false** statement.

options.A: The Europeans were the first to start the slave trade in Africa.
options.B: The slave trade grew with the discovery of the America.
options.C: As many as 12-15 million African slaves were brought to the Americas between the 16th-19th centuries.
options.D: When Europeans first began to take part in the slave trade, they bought slaves from local African merchants.

explanation_steps: Slavery existed in Africa and other parts of the world long before the arrival of Europeans. However, Europeans transformed it into a massive, global commercial enterprise known as the Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade.

questions.stem: Which of the following classes **was not** part of the Third Estate?
explanation_steps: In pre-revolutionary France, the Third Estate represented about 98% of the population. It included everyone who was not a member of the Clergy (First Estate) or the Nobility (Second Estate). Therefore, the bourgeoisie, peasants, lawyers, and doctors were all part of the Third Est

questions.stem: When did Italian colonialism in Eritrea come to an end?
explanation_steps: Italian colonialism in Eritrea effectively ended in **1941** during World War II. Following the decisive Battle of Keren, British and Commonwealth forces defeated the Italian army, leading to the British Military Administration (BMA) of Eritrea.

questions.stem: Identify the one which **was not** part of former Yugoslavia.
explanation_steps: Former Yugoslavia consisted of six republics: **Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia, Montenegro, and Macedonia**. **Slovakia** was part of Czechoslovakia, not Yugoslavia.

questions.stem: To preserve the body after death, ancient Egyptians used a process called __________.
explanation_steps: Ancient Egyptians believed in an afterlife and thought the physical body needed to be preserved for the soul to inhabit it. This complex process of preservation is called **mummification**.

questions.stem: Match the term from Column A with its correct description in Column B: **Machiavelli**

options.I: I. Government dominated by the few

explanation_steps: Niccolò Machiavelli was an Italian diplomat and philosopher during the Renaissance. He is best known for his political treatise **The Prince**, written in $$ 1513 $$, which describes how a ruler should acquire and maintain political power.

questions.stem: What was the aim of the **“Black Consciousness”** movement led by Steve Biko?
questions.answer: To empower Black South Africans to reject psychological oppression and fight for liberation.
accepted_answers: To empower Black South Africans to reject psychological oppression and fight for liberation.
explanation_steps: The Black Consciousness Movement (BCM) aimed to instill pride and self-reliance in Black South Africans. It encouraged them to define themselves and their own values, rejecting the psychological inferiority imposed by the apartheid system, and to unite in the struggle for their o

questions.stem: Which of the following people had a calendar of 12 months and 30 days each?
explanation_steps: The Ancient Egyptians developed a solar calendar consisting of 12 months, each 30 days long, totaling 360 days, with an extra 5 days added at the end of the year to match the solar cycle.

questions.stem: Among the most important developments in medieval Eritrea were

options.A: Turkish and Portuguese attempts to conquer in the 16th century.

explanation_steps: The medieval period in Eritrea saw significant external pressures and internal population movements. The Beja migration (8th-13th centuries) and the 16th-century arrival of the Ottoman Turks and Portuguese were pivotal events.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is **false**?

options.B: Islam accepts Christian and Jewish prophets such as Moses and Jesus Christ.
options.C: When Mohammed began preaching about his revelation, he was accepted quickly.
options.D: Moslems believe that Mohammed received revelation from God.

explanation_steps: When Prophet Mohammed began preaching in Mecca, he was not accepted quickly. He and his followers faced severe persecution and hostility from the Meccan elite, eventually leading to the Hijra (migration to Medina) in 622 AD.

questions.stem: Who was the first to come out with the idea that the sun, not the earth, was the center of the universe?
explanation_steps: Nicolaus Copernicus proposed the Heliocentric theory, which stated that the sun is at the center of the universe and the planets revolve around it, challenging the long-held Geocentric (earth-centered) model.

questions.stem: According to the teachings of Karl Marx,

options.A: the bourgeoisie and the proletariat are two antagonistic classes.
options.B: the state would never wither away.
options.C: all of history is the history of class struggle.
options.D: the bourgeoisie would finally emerge victorious over the proletariat.

explanation_steps: Karl Marx taught that history is driven by class struggle. He identified the bourgeoisie (owners) and proletariat (workers) as opposing classes and predicted that the proletariat would eventually overthrow the bourgeoisie, leading to a classless society where the state would 'wit

questions.stem: Who became the president of **Mähber Fekri Hager** when it was first established?
explanation_steps: When **Mähber Fekri Hager** (Association for the Love of the Country) was established in 1941, **Ghebremeskel Weldu** was elected as its first president. The organization initially aimed to unite Eritreans after the fall of Italian rule.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is **false**?

options.B: The Camp David Accord was an arrangement for an Israeli-Egyptian Peace Treaty.
options.C: During the Six Day War, Israel occupied Arab lands.
options.D: The state of Israel was formed on May 14, 1948.

explanation_steps:
All the statements provided are historically accurate:
- **A:** The Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO) was indeed founded in 1964.
- **B:** The Camp David Accords (1978) led to the 1979 peace treaty between Egypt and Israel.
- **C:** In 1967 (Six-Day War), Israel captured th

questions.stem: The wars between the Romans and Carthaginians were known as __________.
explanation_steps: The **Punic Wars** were a series of three wars fought between Rome and Carthage (264 BC to 146 BC). The name comes from the Latin word 'Punicus', meaning Carthaginian.

questions.stem: Match the term from Column A with its correct description in Column B: **Sputnik**

options.I: I. Government dominated by the few

explanation_steps: **Sputnik 1** was the first artificial Earth satellite. It was launched by the Soviet Union on October $$ 4, 1957 $$. This event triggered the Space Race between the USSR and the USA during the Cold War.

questions.stem: What were the **two** motives behind the Ethiopian economic policies in Eritrea during the period of the Federation?
questions.answer: 1. To weaken Eritrea's economic autonomy. 2. To facilitate eventual annexation.
accepted_answers: 1. To weaken Eritrea's economic autonomy. 2. To facilitate eventual annexation.
explanation_steps:
During the Federation (1952-1962), Ethiopia implemented policies designed to: 
1. **Economic Sabotage:** Weaken Eritrea's industrial base and commercial autonomy to make it economically dependent on Ethiopia.
2. **Political Integration:** Dismantle Eritrean economic institutions

questions.stem: Which of the following **was not** true of Hammurabi's Laws?

options.A: Women had fewer rights and their place was in the home.
options.C: Children were to obey their fathers.
options.D: If a woman failed to bear children, her husband could divorce her.
options.E: Women had equal rights with men.

explanation_steps: Hammurabi's Code was a patriarchal legal system. While it provided some protections, it clearly established that men were superior to women and that women did not have equal rights.

questions.stem: The first colonial influence in Eritrea was by the
explanation_steps: The Ottoman Turks were the first modern colonial power to establish a presence in Eritrea when they occupied Massawa and its surroundings in 1557, establishing the province of Habesh Eyalet.

questions.stem: The successors of prophet Mohammed were called the
explanation_steps: After the death of Prophet Mohammed, the leaders of the Islamic community were known as Caliphs (Khalifa), meaning 'successor' or 'deputy'. The first four are known as the 'Rightly Guided Caliphs'.

questions.stem: Italian expansion into the mainland Eritrea was made possible by the

options.A: famine of 1888-1892 which reduced the ability of people to resist.
options.B: Italian strong pressures against the people.
options.C: local population who were fed up of raids by Ethiopian war lords.

explanation_steps: The 'Kifu Qen' (Great Famine) of 1888-1892 decimated the population and livestock, weakening resistance. Simultaneously, constant raids by Abyssinian/Ethiopian warlords left the local population exhausted and looking for stability.

questions.stem: A scientist who is well-known for his 'Theory of Relativity' is
explanation_steps: Albert Einstein developed the Theory of Relativity (Special and General), which revolutionized our understanding of space, time, gravity, and the universe.

questions.stem: Which of the following was **not** a pro-independence party member in Eritrea?
explanation_steps: **Tedla Bairu** was the leader of the **Unionist Party**, which advocated for the unconditional union of Eritrea with Ethiopia. In contrast, figures like Woldeab Woldemariam and Ibrahim Sultan led parties that fought for Eritrean independence.

questions.stem: The US colony in Southeast Asia was
explanation_steps: The **Philippines** became a US colony following the Spanish-American War in 1898. It remained under US control until it gained independence in 1946.

questions.stem: The worst natural disaster which struck Europe in the Late Middle Ages was known as __________.
explanation_steps: The **Black Death** was a devastating global epidemic of bubonic plague that struck Europe and Asia in the mid-1300s. It killed an estimated 25 million people in Europe alone.

questions.stem: Match the term from Column A with its correct description in Column B: **Bandung**

options.I: I. Government dominated by the few

explanation_steps: The **Bandung Conference** was a meeting of Asian and African states, most of which were newly independent, held in $$ 1955 $$ in Indonesia. It laid the groundwork for the **Non-Aligned Movement**, which sought to remain neutral during the Cold War.

questions.stem: Why did Tigrean chiefs want to expand to Eritrea in the 18th and 19th centuries?
questions.answer: 1. To control Red Sea trade and ports. 2. To collect taxes and tribute.
accepted_answers: 1. To control Red Sea trade and ports. 2. To collect taxes and tribute.
explanation_steps:
Tigrean warlords and chiefs sought expansion into Eritrea for two primary reasons:
1. **Strategic Access:** To control the Red Sea coastline and ports like Massawa, which were vital for international trade and for importing modern firearms.
2. **Revenue and Power:** To increase t

questions.stem: According to the caste system in India, the first caste was the
explanation_steps: In the ancient Indian Varna (caste) system, the Brahmins (priests and scholars) occupied the highest rank, followed by Kshatriyas (warriors).

questions.stem: Which of the following **is not** true of the Nara and Kunama ethnic groups?

options.A: Both were egalitarian communities (everybody was treated equal).
options.B: They belong to a common linguistic family.
options.C: They depend on crop cultivation and animal husbandry.
options.D: They have a closely knit clan administration headed by a council of elders.

explanation_steps: All the statements (A, B, C, and D) are correct descriptions of the Nara and Kunama. They are both Nilotic (Nilo-Saharan) groups, practice mixed farming, and traditionally have egalitarian social structures led by elders.

questions.stem: Which of the following **was not** true of the Maya civilization?

options.A: Agriculture was the basis of the Maya economy.
options.B: The Maya built splendid temples and developed a complicated calendar.
options.C: The Maya civilization flourished between 900-300 B.C. in the Yucatan Peninsula.
options.D: The Maya civilization was not composed of city-states.

explanation_steps: The Maya civilization was organized into independent city-states (like Tikal and Palenque), each ruled by a god-king. They were never unified into a single empire.

questions.stem: In the first phase of their occupation, the Italians wanted to

options.A: use Eritrea as a base to invade Ethiopia.
options.C: create a settlement for Italians in Eritrea.

explanation_steps: Initially, Italy viewed Eritrea as a 'Colonia di Popolamento' (Settler Colony) to solve overpopulation and land hunger in Italy by settling Italian farmers on the fertile Eritrean highlands.

questions.stem: After the French conquest of Indochina, the only remaining free state in southeast Asia was
explanation_steps: Thailand (then known as Siam) was the only Southeast Asian country to avoid European colonization. It served as a 'buffer state' between the British Empire (Burma/Malaya) and the French Empire (Indochina).

questions.stem: The country which was **not** a member of the **Four Great Powers** involved in the future of Eritrea was
explanation_steps: The **Four Great Powers** (or Big Four) responsible for deciding the fate of former Italian colonies after WWII were the **USA, Britain, France, and the Soviet Union (Russia)**. Italy was the defeated colonial power and was not part of this decision-making group.

questions.stem: A country which had to fight a bloody war of independence against the French in North Africa was
explanation_steps: **Algeria** fought a long and brutal war of independence against France from 1954 to 1962. Unlike Tunisia or Morocco, which gained independence relatively peacefully, Algeria was considered an integral part of France, leading to a violent conflict.

questions.stem: The flight of Mohammed from Mecca to Medina is called __________.
explanation_steps: The **Hijra** refers to the journey of the Prophet Muhammad and his followers from Mecca to Medina in 622 AD to escape persecution. This event marks the beginning of the Islamic calendar.

questions.stem: Match the term from Column A with its correct description in Column B: **Knesset**

options.I: I. Government dominated by the few

explanation_steps: The **Knesset** is the unicameral national legislature of **Israel**. It passes all laws, elects the President and Prime Minister, and supervises the work of the government.

questions.stem: The Chinese were responsible for remarkable inventions like
explanation_steps: Ancient China is famous for the 'Four Great Inventions': the compass, gunpowder, papermaking, and printing. These technologies significantly impacted world history.

questions.stem: The Bilen speaking group who moved from Hamasien to the environs of Keren were the
explanation_steps: The Bilen people consist of two main subgroups: Bet Tarke and Bet Tawke. Bet Tawke migrated from Lasta to Hamasien and eventually settled in the Keren area.

questions.stem: In the mid of thirteenth century, Sundiata is considered the founder of the Kingdom of
explanation_steps: Sundiata Keita, known as the 'Lion Prince', founded the Mali Empire in the 13th century after defeating the Soso people at the Battle of Kirina.

questions.stem: The Eritrean patriot who killed Captain Bettini at Walta Medhanit was
explanation_steps: Bahta Hagos, the chief of Akkele-Guzay, led a significant revolt against Italian land alienation in 1894. During the initial confrontation at Walta Medhanit, the Italian officer Captain Bettini was killed.

questions.stem: The state which announced its freedom and became the first independent State in Latin America was
explanation_steps: Haiti became the first independent nation in Latin America and the Caribbean in 1804 following a successful slave revolt against French colonial rule led by Toussaint Louverture and Jean-Jacques Dessalines.

questions.stem: One of the following countries **is not** a member of **NATO**.
explanation_steps: **Austria** is a neutral country and is not a member of NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organization). Belgium, France, Denmark, and Norway were all founding members or early joiners of the alliance.

questions.stem: Who was the first president of Guinea when it became independent in 1958?
explanation_steps: **Ahmed Sékou Touré** was the first President of Guinea. In 1958, Guinea was the only French colony in Africa to vote for immediate independence, rejecting Charles de Gaulle's proposal for a French Community.

questions.stem: One of the Dahlak Islands, which was used as a prison by the Italians was __________.
explanation_steps: The island of **Nokra**, part of the Dahlak Archipelago, was used by the Italian colonial administration as a notorious detention camp for Eritrean and Ethiopian political prisoners.

questions.stem: Match the term from Column A with its correct description in Column B: **Marx and Engles**

options.I: I. Government dominated by the few

explanation_steps: Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels were German philosophers who co-authored the **Communist Manifesto** in $$ 1848 $$. This document outlined the theory of class struggle and the eventual overthrow of capitalism by the working class.

questions.stem: Find the sentence which **is not** true.

options.A: Hinduism believes in the idea of reincarnation.
options.B: According to the teachings of Buddha, life is full of suffering.
options.C: Buddha teaches that people should not kill and should not steal.
options.D: The most important religious practice of Buddha is yoga or meditation.
options.E: Hinduism has created a legacy of equality in Indian societies.

explanation_steps: Hinduism is associated with the caste system, which is a rigid social hierarchy. Therefore, it did not create a legacy of equality; rather, it institutionalized social inequality based on birth.

questions.stem: A notorious and brutal Abyssinian warlord who tortured people by putting hot roasted peas into their ears was
explanation_steps: Ras Wube Hailemariam of Semien was notorious for his frequent and brutal raids into the Eritrean highlands during the mid-19th century. He is remembered in oral tradition for his extreme cruelty.

questions.stem: Identify the **correct** statement.

options.A: Over the period of two millennia the Bantu spread all over Sub-Saharan Africa.
options.B: Intermarriage was common among the African and Arab ruling groups.
options.C: Swahili combines Bantu and Arabic words and phrases.
options.D: The kingdom of Ghana was the first great trading state in West Africa as early as 500 B.C.

explanation_steps: All statements are correct: The Bantu migration lasted 2,000 years; Arab-African intermarriage occurred along the Swahili coast; Swahili is a blend of Bantu and Arabic; and Ghana was the first major West African trade empire.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is **correct**?

options.A: Bahta Hagos was killed at the Battle of Halay.
options.B: Mohammed Nurri had plans to enter Asmara and kill Ferdinando Martini.
options.C: Abubeker Ahmed was a Saho leader who led a force of Saho and Tigrigna fighters against the Italians.

explanation_steps: All these statements are historically accurate. Bahta Hagos died at Halay. Mohammed Nurri (a Saho leader) plotted against Governor Martini. Abubeker Ahmed also led a multi-ethnic resistance force against Italian rule.

questions.stem: The part of Africa which had been affected more by the slave trade was
explanation_steps: West Africa was the primary source for the Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade. Millions of Africans were captured from this region and transported to the Americas to work on plantations.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is **correct**?

options.A: Berlin Wall became a symbol of division in the Cold War period.
options.B: The first man-made space satellite was sent by the USA.
options.D: Yugoslavia was a member of the Warsaw Pact.
options.E: During the Bay of Pigs Invasion, US forces defeated Cuba.

explanation_steps:
Statement A is correct. The **Berlin Wall** (built in 1961) was the most prominent physical symbol of the division between the democratic West and the communist East during the Cold War. 
* B is wrong: USSR sent the first satellite (Sputnik).
* C is wrong: NATO was established in

questions.stem: Which of the following countries was recipient of Soviet aid during the Cold War era?
explanation_steps: During the Cold War, the Soviet Union provided military and economic aid to various African nations with socialist leanings. **Mozambique (FRELIMO), Ethiopia (under the Derg), Somalia (under Siad Barre initially), and Angola (MPLA)** were all major recipients of Soviet support.

questions.stem: One of the following **was not** included in Confucius's teachings.

options.A: Governments should be limited to men of noble birth.
options.B: Parents should love their children, and children should obey their parents.
options.C: Husbands should fulfill their duties, and wives should be obedient.
options.D: Rulers should be kind to their subjects; subjects should be loyal to their rulers.

explanation_steps: Confucius believed that government service should be open to all men of talent and virtue, not just those of noble birth. This led to the development of the civil service examination system in China.

questions.stem: In the 18th and 19th centuries, the Tigreans wanted to expand into Eritrea in order to

options.A: collect taxes and tribute from the Eritrean people.
options.B: get access to the coast so as to obtain arms from abroad.
options.C: help them benefit from Red Sea trade.

explanation_steps: Expansionist efforts by Tigrean lords were driven by economic and strategic needs: extracting resources (taxes), controlling trade routes to the Red Sea, and securing a path to import modern firearms from Europe.

questions.stem: Which of the following places **was not** part of the Central African Kingdom?
explanation_steps: Ghana was a kingdom located in West Africa, not Central Africa. Luba, Lunda (Lundi), and Kongo (Congo) were prominent kingdoms in the Central African region.

questions.stem: In the administration of justice, the Italians used the civil code for

options.A: cases in which at least one of the partners was an Italian citizen.
options.B: civil cases where the parties were Eritreans.

explanation_steps: The Italian colonial legal system was dualistic. The Italian Civil Code applied to Italians and assimilated foreigners. Eritreans were generally subject to customary and religious laws administered by local chiefs or cadis.

questions.stem: Which of the following countries **was not** part of the Central Powers in World War I?
explanation_steps: Russia was part of the Allied Powers (Triple Entente) along with Britain and France. The Central Powers consisted of Germany, Austria-Hungary, the Ottoman Empire (Turkey), and Bulgaria.

questions.stem: The West opposed Egypt's President, General Abdel Nasser's, foreign policies because of his

options.A: formal recognition of the People's Republic of China.
options.B: support of anti-colonial movements in Kenya and Algeria.
options.C: signing an arms deal with Czechoslovakia.
options.D: role as a co-founder of the non-aligned movement.

explanation_steps: Western powers (especially the US, UK, and France) opposed **Gamal Abdel Nasser** for all these reasons. His recognition of Communist China, support for African independence movements, arms deals with the Soviet bloc (Czechoslovakia), and leadership in the Non-Aligned Movement we

questions.stem: The resolution of the Adobha Conference called for

options.A: holding of a national conference within one year.
options.B: the formation of a preparatory committee for the national conference.
options.C: the appointment of a committee to investigate the misdeeds.

explanation_steps: The **Adobha Conference (1969)** was a critical meeting within the ELF (Eritrean Liberation Front) to address internal crises. Its resolutions included investigating past mistakes, forming a preparatory committee, and planning for a general national congress.

questions.stem: Give **two** reasons for the decline of the Axumite Kingdom.
questions.answer: 1. Rise of Islam and loss of Red Sea trade. 2. Environmental degradation.
accepted_answers: 1. Rise of Islam and loss of Red Sea trade. 2. Environmental degradation.
explanation_steps:
The decline of Axum was caused by several factors:
1. **Rise of Islam:** The expansion of Islam in the 7th century led to the loss of control over Red Sea trade routes, isolating Axum economically.
2. **Environmental Degradation:** Over-farming and deforestation led to soil exhau

questions.stem: The philosophy in China, which believed that human beings are evil by nature and therefore require a strong ruler to create peace and order in society, is
explanation_steps: Legalism was a Chinese philosophy that argued humans are inherently selfish and evil. To maintain order, a ruler must use strict laws and harsh punishments.

questions.stem: The first European university was established in
explanation_steps: The University of Bologna, founded in 1088 in Italy, is recognized as the oldest university in continuous operation in the world.

questions.stem: The famous trading city found in the Malian Kingdom was
explanation_steps: Timbuktu was the most famous city of the Mali Empire. It was a major center for the trans-Saharan trade and a world-renowned center of Islamic learning and culture.

questions.stem: Who was the first president of the U.S.A?
explanation_steps: George Washington, the commander-in-chief of the Continental Army during the American Revolutionary War, became the first President of the United States in 1789.

questions.stem: Which of the following points **was not** included in President Woodrow Wilson's fourteen points plan?

options.A: Germany to pay huge amount of war reparation
options.C: Formation of the League of Nations
options.D: Continuation of secret treaties between countries
options.E: Free access to international waters by all countries

explanation_steps: Woodrow Wilson's 14 Points aimed for a 'just and lasting peace'. One of his key principles was 'Open covenants of peace, openly arrived at', which explicitly called for an end to secret treaties (secret diplomacy).

questions.stem: The East European country, which was invaded by the Soviets in 1968, was
explanation_steps: In **1968**, the Soviet Union and its Warsaw Pact allies invaded **Czechoslovakia** to crush the 'Prague Spring,' a period of political liberalization and reform led by Alexander Dubček.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is **true**?

options.A: The Eritrean Liberation Movement was formed in Port Sudan in 1958.
options.B: Osman Salih Sabbe was the chairperson of the Eritrean Liberation Front when it was formed in Cairo.
options.C: The Eritrean Liberation Movement attacked the Eritrean Liberation Front at Ela Tsada in 1965.
options.D: The establishment of the zonal commands in Eritrea was taken from the experience of Vietnam.

explanation_steps:
Statement A is historically correct: The **Eritrean Liberation Movement (ELM)**, also known as *Mahber Shewate*, was founded in **Port Sudan in 1958**. 
- B is false: Idris Mohammed Adem was the key figure in the initial leadership.
- C is false: The ELF actually liquidated the E

questions.stem: What were the **three** aims or objectives of Italian colonial policy in Eritrea?
explanation_steps:
Italy's objectives in Eritrea included:
1. **Strategic Base:** To use Eritrea as a springboard for further expansion into the Horn of Africa, especially Ethiopia.
2. **Settlement:** To settle surplus Italian population in the highlands of Eritrea.
3. **Economic Exploitation:** To

questions.stem: The Greek philosopher, who said that the three types of good government were monarchy, aristocracy and constitutional government, was
explanation_steps: Aristotle analyzed various city-states and concluded that there are three good forms of government (monarchy, aristocracy, and constitutional/polity) and three bad forms (tyranny, oligarchy, and democracy/mob rule).

questions.stem: Which of the following comes **first** chronologically?
explanation_steps: Australopithecus (Australo phicin) is the earliest genus in the human evolutionary timeline among the choices, dating back over 4 million years. Homo erectus and Homo sapiens appeared much later.

questions.stem: The period of Renaissance was characterized by

options.A: the fact that it was largely an urban phenomenon where powerful city-states became the centers of political, economic and social lives.
options.B: being an age of recovery from the disasters of the 14th Century.

explanation_steps: The Renaissance (rebirth) began in Italian city-states. It was a recovery from the Black Death and political instability of the 1300s, and it emphasized Humanism—the focus on human potential and individual achievement.

questions.stem: One of the following persons **was not** associated with Italian unification.
explanation_steps: Otto von Bismarck was the 'Iron Chancellor' responsible for the unification of Germany, not Italy. Cavour, Garibaldi, and Mazzini are the key figures of the Italian Risorgimento (unification).

questions.stem: The Second World War started on September 1, 1939, when German forces attacked
explanation_steps: The invasion of Poland by Nazi Germany on September 1, 1939, is the event that directly led Britain and France to declare war on Germany, marking the official start of World War II.

questions.stem: The idea of **'Perestroika'** or structural policy was associated with
explanation_steps: **Perestroika** (restructuring) and **Glasnost** (openness) were the two landmark reform policies introduced by **Mikhail Gorbachev** in the mid-1980s to modernize the Soviet economy and political system.

questions.stem: Identify the **false** statement.

options.A: The Nadew Command was destroyed in 1988.
options.B: The Fenkil Operation refers to the liberation of Massawa.
options.C: The third EPLF Congress took place in 1987.
options.E: The EPLF supported the EPRDF to enter Addis-Abeba.

explanation_steps: Statement C is false because the **Second Congress** of the EPLF took place in 1987. The Third Congress (which transformed EPLF into PFDJ) took place in **1994**.

questions.stem: What were the **two** reasons for the expansion of Islam in the 7th century?
questions.answer: 1. Military conquest. 2. Trade and religious appeal.
accepted_answers: 1. Military conquest. 2. Trade and religious appeal.
explanation_steps:
1. **Military Conquest:** The early Caliphates successfully defeated the weakened Byzantine and Persian Empires.
2. **Religious Appeal and Trade:** Islam's message of equality and justice appealed to many, and Muslim merchants spread the faith along trade routes.

questions.stem: The European country that was the leader in European exploration was
explanation_steps: Portugal was the pioneer of the Age of Discovery under the leadership of Prince Henry the Navigator. They were the first to explore the coast of Africa and find a sea route to India.

questions.stem: Which of the following **was not** a characteristic feature of the Byzantine Empire?

options.A: The Church came to be known as the Eastern Orthodox Church.
options.B: The patriarch, and not the king, occupied a crucial position in the Empire.
options.C: The Byzantine Empire was both a Greek and Church state.
options.D: Greek was the official language of the Empire.

explanation_steps: In the Byzantine Empire, the Emperor (Basileus) held supreme authority over both the state and the church (a system known as Caesaropapism). While the Patriarch was the spiritual leader, the Emperor was the ultimate political and religious head.

questions.stem: The first explorer who reached the Americas in 1492 was
explanation_steps: Christopher Columbus, sailing for Spain, reached the Caribbean islands in 1492 while searching for a westward sea route to Asia. This marked the beginning of sustained European contact with the Americas.

questions.stem: Which of the following events happened **first** in connection with the French Revolution?

options.A: The meeting of the Estates General
options.C: The crowning of Napoleon as Emperor
options.D: The end of the reign of terror

explanation_steps: The meeting of the Estates General in May 1789 was the event that triggered the revolution. The Storming of the Bastille followed in July 1789.

questions.stem: The U.S.A joined the Second World War because

options.A: it feared that Britain would be defeated by the Germans.
options.C: it wanted to save the world from communist domination.
options.D: it wanted to emerge as the strongest power in the world.

explanation_steps: The United States maintained neutrality until December 7, 1941, when Japan launched a surprise military strike against the U.S. naval base at Pearl Harbor, Hawaii. The U.S. declared war on Japan the next day.

questions.stem: The Eritrean referendum was conducted on
explanation_steps: The Eritrean independence referendum was held from **April 23 to 25, 1993**. The results showed 99.83% in favor of independence, which was officially declared on May 24, 1993.
